questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations

questions.evidence: ethical_reviews: Study approved by IRB of University of Washington (approval number STUDY00016228) with reliance agreements from UAB and UCSD. informed_consent: Written informed consent from all participants, consent process developed with bioethics guidance and reviewed by Community Advisory Board. is_deidentified: Public access dataset is de-identified with sensitive PHI moved to controlled access, de-identification procedures follow applicable regulations, AI-READI Data License Agreement prohibits re-identification. at_risk_populations: Bioethics guidance from co-investigators, Community Advisory Board of 11 persons with diversity oversight, exclusion of pregnant individuals.

questions.name: Interoperability and Standardization
questions.description: Presence of standard formats and schema conformance
questions.evidence: distribution_formats: DICOM (retinal imaging), CSV (tabular/time-series), mHealth standard (wearable data converted from .FIT), XML (ECG). preprocessing_strategies[4]: 'All data mapped to applicable data standard formats such as Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model for clinical data and DICOM format for retinal imaging. Data stored and shared as AI-ready enabling immediate AI/ML research without reformatting.' preprocessing_strategies[1]: Image format conversion from proprietary (.fda, .sdt) to DICOM standard.

Conversion from proprietary formats to standards demonstrates commitment to interoperability. AI-ready data enables immediate use without reformatting.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing libraries or tools
questions.score_label: At least one preprocessing tool listed
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods mention data collection tools (REDCap, Dexcom G6, Garmin VivoSmart 5, Aurora IQ, EIDON, Spectralis, Maestro2, Triton DRI OCT, Cirrus 5000, FLIO, Electronic Visual Acuity tester, Mars chart, Topcon KR 800, Philips Pagewriter TC30, MoCA Duo Application) but no explicit software_and_tools field documenting preprocessing software. preprocessing_strategies mention 'standardized operating procedures' and format conversions but not specific preprocessing software libraries or versions.
questions.quality_note: Data collection instruments are well documented but preprocessing/analysis software tools, libraries, and versions are not explicitly documented. This gap limits technical reproducibility for data processing workflows.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.description: Description completeness of participant recruitment and data acquisition
questions.score_label: Full recruitment and procedural details included
questions.evidence: collection_mechanisms: 5 detailed mechanisms including (1) in-person visits at 3 sites lasting 2.5-4 hours with multi-domain protocol, (2) EHR screening using ICD-10 codes (E11.X for T2DM, R73.09 for pre-diabetes) for patients aged 40+ with medical encounters 2020-2025, (3) wave-based recruitment to maintain triple-balanced sampling, (4) home-based wearable monitoring over 10 days, (5) biospecimen collection and centralized biobanking at UAB CCTS. acquisition_methods: 12 detailed methods covering survey/questionnaire (REDCap), physical measurements, retinal imaging (7 devices), visual function, clinical labs (local CLIA + central UW NORC), ECG, cognitive function (MoCA), peripheral neuropathy, continuous glucose monitoring, physical activity, environmental monitoring, biospecimen collection. data_collectors: Trained certified study coordinators at 3 sites following Manual of Procedures with certification process and practice subjects. sampling_strategies: Triple-balanced recruitment with targeted under/oversampling, personalized invitations via REDCap.
questions.quality_note: Exceptionally comprehensive collection protocol documentation covering complete recruitment pipeline (EHR screening to enrollment), detailed procedural protocols for 12+ data acquisition methods with specific instruments and parameters, multi-site coordination procedures, and quality control measures. Provides reproducible roadmap for study replication.

questions.name: Version History Documentation

questions.evidence: distribution_dates: 4 versioned releases with dates: (1) Pilot data released May 2024, (2) v1.0.0 data through July 31, 2024 released November 2024, (3) v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 released with additional participants, (4) Final dataset expected after 4,000 participant enrollment by November 2026. version_access: 'All prior versions of the dataset are maintained with version-specific documentation at https://docs.aireadi.org/. Each version includes a changelog and data dictionary. Dataset versioning uses semantic versioning (e.g., v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0).' updates: 'Dataset updated periodically as enrollment progresses toward target of 4,000 participants by November 2026. Version-specific documentation maintained for each release.'
questions.quality_note: Excellent version history with 4+ documented releases, semantic versioning (v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0), specific release dates, version-specific documentation with changelogs and data dictionaries at persistent URL, and clear ongoing release schedule tied to enrollment milestones.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.description: Inclusion of demographics and subgroup details
questions.evidence: instances: 'Individual participants aged 40 and older with and without Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Target enrollment is 4,000 people, triple-balanced by self-reported race/ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White), T2DM severity (no diabetes, pre-diabetes/lifestyle-controlled, medication-controlled, insulin-controlled), and biological sex (male, female). Participants must speak, read, and understand English. Exclusion criteria include pregnancy and type 1 diabetes.' subpopulations: 8 detailed subgroups - 4 race/ethnicity groups (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White each ~1,000, 25%), 4 diabetes severity groups (no diabetes, pre-diabetes/lifestyle-controlled, medication-controlled, insulin-controlled each ~1,000, 25%). sampling_strategies: Triple-balanced recruitment design critical for unbiased AI/ML, volunteer selection acknowledged as source of potential bias limiting generalizability.
questions.quality_note: Exceptionally detailed human subject representation with comprehensive demographics (age, race/ethnicity, sex, diabetes severity), quantified subpopulation targets, explicit inclusion criteria (age 40+, English-speaking) and exclusion criteria (pregnancy, type 1 diabetes), acknowledgment of sampling limitations (volunteer bias), and rationale for sampling design (AI/ML fairness).

strengths: Exceptional structural completeness with all mandatory fields populated and 19 diverse keywords providing comprehensive topic coverage
Outstanding funding documentation including multiple grant numbers, funding amounts, and project timeline exceeding standard requirements

Comprehensive ethical documentation covering IRB approval (STUDY00016228), informed consent with bioethics oversight, de-identification procedures, and Community Advisory Board engagement for at-risk populations
Clear two-tier access model with CC BY-NC 4.0 for public data and separate DUA for controlled access, including explicit permitted and prohibited uses
Excellent interoperability with multiple standard formats (DICOM, CSV, mHealth, XML) and OMOP Common Data Model conformance for clinical data
Exceptionally detailed collection protocol documentation covering recruitment pipeline, 12+ acquisition methods with specific instruments, multi-site coordination, and quality control
Strong version history with semantic versioning (v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0), timestamped releases, changelogs, and version-specific documentation
Multiple DOI-linked publications (BMJ Open, Nature Metabolism, Zenodo) plus dataset DOI enabling bidirectional discovery
Comprehensive human subject representation with quantified subpopulation targets, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and acknowledgment of sampling limitations

Outstanding FAIRness with persistent identifiers (DOI, landing page), fully defined access mechanisms, clear license terms, structured provenance tracking, and cross-platform interlinking (FAIRhub, Bridge2AI, NIH RePORTER, Zenodo, journals)
weaknesses: No quantitative file size or dimensional metadata limiting resource planning and discoverability (Question 5)

Limited preprocessing software documentation - data collection instruments are well documented but preprocessing libraries, software versions, and analysis tools are not explicitly enumerated (Question 11)
recommendations: Add file size metadata for distributions (e.g., ZIP archive sizes, total dataset size) and dimensional metadata for data arrays (e.g., number of DICOM images, CSV row counts, time-series lengths) to aid resource planning and dataset evaluation

Create explicit software_and_tools documentation listing preprocessing and analysis software with versions (e.g., image format conversion tools with versions, OMOP mapping software, data harmonization scripts, quality control software) to enhance technical reproducibility
Consider documenting computational requirements or recommended specifications for working with the full dataset given its multimodal nature and 4,000 participant scale
